doc.title: Tom Baker interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: Carrying multiple instruments on flights
summary: The burden of travelling with several horns and getting them past airline staff.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Okay. Well good. I just want you to stay healthy now.
To carry all those instruments around.
It’s the worst thing about being a multi-instrumentalist. You’ve got to carry them.
Yeah. Especially when you’re coming from there to here, and back and planes and all that kind of stuff.

Yeah. I’ve got one bag with my clothes and CDs. And then you’ve got an option — you have to take no more than two bags. So trombone is bag number two. And then you’ve got to carry the others on your shoulders and do some fast explaining at the door about why you’ve got three cases, and none of them fit in the little thing, and you say “well please, my livelihood depends on this and won’t you put it in the suit closet?” And they take pity on you. But you’re always doing this.
So it helps if you wear a tie and don’t look like a bum.
